challenges.text: Learn the names of five people you meet or see today. Recall all five before bed.
Build a memory palace from ten spots in your home. Store today's to-do list there and recall it without notes tonight.
Take a problem you're stuck on. Write only the facts you're certain of, then build a solution up from those.
Read 20 pages of nonfiction. Write two sentences on what you'll do differently because of it.
Explain one idea you learned this week to someone in under two minutes. If you stumble, reread it.
Write down a belief you hold strongly, then the best argument against it.
Do 15 minutes of chess tactics with the engine off. Write down the one pattern you missed.
Read one explainer on a physics or engineering idea and summarize it in a single sentence.
Learn one new word and use it in conversation before dinner.
Sit somewhere public for ten minutes. Guess one person's job from what you can see, then note what gave it away.
100 push-ups today, in as many sets as it takes.
Throw one punch or kick 200 times, slowly, with clean form. Quality over speed.
Stretch for 15 minutes tonight: hips, hamstrings and shoulders.
Get outside within an hour of waking and spend ten minutes in daylight.
Walk 8,000 steps. Do at least one walk with the phone left at home.
No food in the two hours before bed.
Hold a plank for your best time, then try to add ten seconds.
End your shower with 60 seconds of cold water.
Pick a bedtime and keep it tonight. Screens off for the last 30 minutes.
Train legs today. Squats or lunges, whatever you have, until the last set is hard.
Track your water today and get to about three liters.
In your next three conversations, hold eye contact a beat longer than feels normal.
Ask someone what they really want out of this year. Then listen without giving advice.
Go the whole day without saying anything you don't mean, including polite white lies.
Dress one notch sharper than the day calls for.
Notice something about a friend or coworker you've never noticed before, and mention it kindly.
Talk 10% slower today. Pause for a second before you answer questions.
Record yourself explaining something for 60 seconds. Watch it once and fix one thing.
Compliment one person specifically. Name what they did, not just that it was good.
Check your posture every two hours. Set a reminder so you actually do it.
Wash your face and moisturize tonight. Sunscreen tomorrow morning, even if it's cloudy.
Floss tonight.
If it's been more than four weeks since your last haircut, book one today.
Clear and wipe down your desk for ten minutes.
Cook one meal yourself today with real protein and a vegetable.
Iron or steam tomorrow's clothes tonight.
Work one 90-minute block with notifications off and the phone in another room.
No social media until noon. Check the Today section here instead.
Do your hardest task before you open messages.
Before bed, write the two tasks that would make tomorrow a good day.
Mute or delete one app or account that leaves you feeling worse after you use it.
Finish one thing you started and dropped.
Admit one mistake out loud today and say what you'll do about it.
Spend 30 minutes on a hard skill you're bad at: piano, a language, a new kind of code.
Build or repair something with your hands for 30 minutes.
Say no to one request that doesn't fit your goals.
Do one useful thing for someone and don't mention it.

quotes.q: Absorb what is useful, discard what is useless and add what is specifically your own.
I fear not the man who has practiced 10,000 kicks once, but I fear the man who has practiced one kick 10,000 times.
Knowing is not enough, we must apply. Willing is not enough, we must do.
Mistakes are always forgivable, if one has the courage to admit them.
If you spend too much time thinking about a thing, you'll never get it done.
Do not pray for an easy life, pray for the strength to endure a difficult one.
When something is important enough, you do it even if the odds are not in your favor.
Persistence is very important. You should not give up unless you are forced to give up.
I think it's very important to have a feedback loop, where you're constantly thinking about what you've done and how you could be doing it better.
What is it you truly desire?
